questions.question: What is the main characteristic of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: It slows down the reaction and is chemically altered.
It speeds up the reaction and is completely used up.
It speeds up the reaction without being used up or chemically changed.
It initiates a reaction but changes into a different substance.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about catalysts is true?
options: A single catalyst can speed up any chemical reaction.
Different reactions require different, specific catalysts.
Catalysts only work for reactions involving gases.
Catalysts must be liquids to function properly.

questions.question: What are enzymes?
options: Biological catalysts that speed up reactions in living cells.
Synthetic chemicals used to harden plastics.
Non-reactive proteins that slow down digestion.
Minerals found in metal ores.

questions.question: In a displacement reaction in solution, what occurs when a more reactive metal is added?
options: It displaces a less reactive metal from its salt.
It combines with a less reactive metal to form an alloy.
It dissolves without any chemical change.
It prevents any other chemical reactions from happening.

questions.question: What are the products when magnesium is added to copper sulfate solution?
options: Magnesium oxide and copper sulfate
Magnesium sulfate and copper
Copper magnesium and sulfur
Magnesium hydroxide and copper oxide

questions.question: How can displacement reactions be useful in studying metals?
options: They are used to determine the melting point of metals.
They can confirm the position of a metal in the reactivity series.
They are the only way to turn non-metals into metals.
They allow metals to be stretched into thin wires.

questions.question: When can carbon be used to extract a metal from its ore?
options: Only when carbon is more reactive than the metal.
Only when the metal is extremely unreactive like gold.
Only when carbon is less reactive than the metal.
When the metal ore is a liquid at room temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the typical properties of metals?
options: Poor conductors of heat, brittle, and dull.
High density, gaseous at room temperature, and highly acidic.
Good thermal and electrical conductors, strong, shiny, and malleable.
Soft substances that become brittle only when heated.

questions.question: How are ceramics made, and how do their properties change?
options: They are made from liquid polymers that become flexible when cooled.
They are made from soft substances that become hard and brittle when heated.
They are made by mixing metals to form a flexible alloy.
They are made from gases that solidify into highly conductive sheets.

questions.question: What is an alloy?
options: Pure metal elements with no impurities.
A mixture of elements including at least one metal.
A composite material made entirely of plastics.
A compound formed when a metal reacts with oxygen.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of creating a composite material?
options: To combine materials to create a new material with improved properties.
To break down polymers into their original monomers.
To make a material more reactive with acids.
To turn a metal into a highly brittle ceramic.

questions.question: What are polymers made of?
options: Small molecules called monomers that join together to form very long chains of atoms.
Large metallic crystals held together by ionic bonds.
Mixtures of different metals melted together.
Soft clay particles heated to high temperatures.

questions.question: What effect does a plasticiser have when added to a polymer?
options: It creates strong cross-links, making the polymer extremely rigid.
It gets between polymer molecules and allows them to move over each other more easily.
It causes the polymer to break down rapidly into individual monomers.
It increases the melting point by making molecules harder to separate.

questions.question: How do cross-links between polymer molecules affect a polymer's properties?
options: They make the polymer much softer and easier to melt.
They make the polymer harder and less flexible.
They turn the polymer into an electrical conductor.
They allow the molecules to slide past each other very easily.

questions.question: What is produced when certain metals react with an acid?
options: A metal hydroxide and oxygen gas.
A metal oxide and water.
A metal salt and hydrogen gas.
A carbonate and nitrogen gas.

questions.question: What products are formed when some metals react with water?
options: A metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
A metal oxide and carbon dioxide.
A metal salt and oxygen gas.
A pure non-metal and steam.

questions.question: What does the reactivity series for metals show?
options: How much heat a metal can conduct compared to others.
How vigorously metals react, compared to each other.
The order of metals by their density.
The year in which each metal was discovered.

questions.question: How does a metal's position in the reactivity series relate to its reactions?
options: The higher the position of a metal, the more vigorously it is likely to react.
The higher the position of a metal, the less likely it is to react.
The lower the position of a metal, the faster it reacts with cold water.
The position of a metal has no relationship to how it reacts.
